text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired -> PD: #SRE-High: multiple 502/SSL handshake errs (us-east-1)

pagerduty: Incident triggered by monitoring: lb-edge-us-east target health degradation > 30% (auto-escalate in 5m). Alert id PD-8723

raj patel: acked PD-8723 :hand: I'm on it, looking at LB/target groups now

alice chen: joining — any customer reports yet? which frontends impacted?

maria gonzalez: internal alerting + top-of-funnel 502 spikes from synthetic checks and some customer sessions failing TLS handshake. Region: us-east-1 primary edge pool

kyle hamm: seeing increased 525/526 and SSL errors in edge-proxy logs. sample from 2026-03-15T12:03:22Z:
```
[edge-proxy] conn=0x7ff TLS handshake failed: alert handshake_failure (SNI mismatch)
[upstream] target ip=10.12.5.23 health=Unhealthy check=/healthz status=502
```

sam oncall: confirm health check path still /healthz? recent deploy changed health endpoints yesterday right?

deploy-bot: Deployment: service=edge-proxy canary v3.14.2 -> v3.15.0 at 2026-03-15T06:41Z by ci-cd

raj patel: good call — checking target group configs vs the new image

alice chen: start impact assessment: which customers routed to us-east? cart-service + api-gateway-legacy have sticky routing there, might affect sessions. We should classify P1 if customer-facing auth/api failing.

maria gonzalez: early data: 12% of global traffic hitting errors, most concentrated in us-east. Synthetic failure rate 37% across edge endpoints. I'd mark as P1 for now.

kyle hamm: running aws elbv2 describe-target-health for tg-edge-us-east...
```
> Target: i-0abcde12345 10.12.5.23 -> Unhealthy (Health check failed, status code 502)
> Target: i-0fghij67890 10.12.5.24 -> Unhealthy (TLS handshake error)
> Target: i-0klmn45678 10.12.5.25 -> Healthy
```

raj patel: two unhealthy, one healthy. Looks like canary nodes failed health checks. Rolling restart maybe? First, shift traffic away from us-east to us-west as a mitigation.

alice chen: agree. Prepare weight-shift to 0.2 for us-east, move 80% to us-west. Use traffic-manager route weights. @maria can you validate downstream capacity in us-west?

maria gonzalez: us-west has headroom for +80% for short window. I'll watch. starting weight-shift now.

maria gonzalez: (action) route-weight update: edge-route-global -> us-east:0.2, us-west:0.8 :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Route change executed by maria.gonzalez at 2026-03-15T12:08:12Z

raj patel: after shift, 502 rate dropped from 37% -> 8% in synthetic checks. Good.

kyle hamm: still seeing SSL handshake_failure on some sessions that still hit us-east. Investigating certs and SNI matching on canary build.

raj patel: grabbed a canary instance: docker exec edge-proxy cat /etc/edge/config | grep health || true

raj patel: config shows health_path=/live (NOT /healthz). ah — canary changed health endpoint but LB health-check still /healthz.

alice chen: that's our culprit. Why didn't CI catch this? Deploy pipeline should have validated LB health path compatibility.

sam oncall: quick fix options: 1) update target group health check path to /live, 2) roll back canary to previous image, 3) update canary to add /healthz route

maria gonzalez: updating TG health path is fastest, but affects all targets; safer to rollback canary from the service group.

kyle hamm: rollback initiated for canary subset -> reverting edge-proxy v3.15.0 to v3.14.2 on canary nodes

deploy-bot: Rollback started: service=edge-proxy canary rollback to v3.14.2 (triggered by kyle)

raj patel: restarting the two unhealthy targets after rollback

raj patel: aws elbv2 register-targets -> re-register i-0abcde12345 and i-0fghij67890

kyle hamm: monitoring health checks... looks like both came back: status=Healthy

maria gonzalez: synthetic checks back to baseline ~1.2% errors. Customer-reported incidents dropping. Marking mitigated for now.

alice chen: good. Let's keep the incident open until all checks stable for 30m and PD auto-resolves. We should also gather timeline + RCA notes.

sam oncall: handoff to raj for postmortem writeup. @raj please include: root cause (health path change in canary), detection (monitoring + PD alerts), mitigation (traffic weight shift, rollback), follow-ups (add CI health-path test, add canary LB config verification), customer comms draft.

raj patel: ack — I'll take PM for postmortem. Drafting now.

pagerduty: PD-8723 acknowledged by raj patel at 2026-03-15T12:11:00Z. No further escalation.

incident-bot: Incident status: Mitigated (partial) — monitoring until 2026-03-15T12:40:00Z for auto-close

alice chen: quick customer impact note: affected sessions ~12% from 11:40-12:08 UTC, main symptom 502/TLS handshake failures for API clients. Recommend notif to support with short blurb: "Intermittent API errors for US-East customers due to deployment issue; mitigated by traffic shift + rollback; monitoring continues." @maria can you send?

maria gonzalez: sending now to #support and #customer-notify. cc: sales if any high-touch customers flagged.

sam oncall: adding follow-ups: 1) CI job to check LB health-path compatibility (owner: infra CI team), 2) update deployment runbook for canary to include health-path validation and LB shrink/expand steps, 3) dashboard alert tuning to reduce noisy auto-escalation thresholds.

raj patel: timeline note for postmortem: detection 12:03, PD page 12:04, traffic shift 12:08, rollback complete 12:10, mitigated 12:11. Will add logs & commands.

alice chen: nice. please include the exact commands in the postmortem (register/unregister, route-weight change) for reproducibility.

raj patel: will do. closing interim updates — will post final postmortem link here when ready.

incident-bot: PD-8723 status changed to resolved at 2026-03-15T12:41:00Z (auto-resolve)

pagerduty: Incident PD-8723 resolved by system at 2026-03-15T12:41:00Z

maria gonzalez: postmortem draft: https://redwood-internal/pm/postmortems/PD-8723-draft (will iterate)

kyle hamm: added a quick hotfix PR to add a CI check: CI: verify-health-path-matches-lb (reviewers: infra-ci)

sam oncall: thanks everyone. good quick coordination. :thumbsup:
